lines.text: highest blessing of all, namely that which confers fulfilment
on our life, can always be only a gift and never the satisfac-
tion of a claim, a due, arrogantly asserted.
And how much joy, what stores of blessing, are missed by
a nation's youth which supposes that it has a rightful claim
to the satisfaction of its wishes! We are of course always
hearing it said: "I have a right to my body." No! You have
no right to it; your body is a gift entrusted to you by the
Creator, a gift which it is your duty to keep whole and pure.
And whoever takes as right what should be a gift, inevitably
misses the most precious things in life. Naturally readiness for
a gift implies also readiness for renunciation. Only he who
is prepared to renounce, to surrender all claimfulness, has
the power for unhindered receptiveness. And if what he
receives is not what he has desired and longed for, then the
unexpected gift which is granted him will be for him an un-
expected source of blessing and happiness, and he will learn
to understand his very renunciation, unavoidable as it was,
to be a gift of grace.
In human society there is of course an assertion of right,
without which it would be impossible for men to live in
community. That, however, is never a question of my right
and your right, but of intrinsic rightfulness for which each
one must be answerable. And human society can only be
sound when the individual is concerned not so much about
his own claims as about his duties and obligations. Moreover
even this is far too little. Human society subsists not only on a
basis of sense of obligation, but also on the basis of love and
mutual trust. It can exist and thrive only when the individual
is prepared to renounce and sacrifice himself for the sake of
another; when its members are not nervously anxious to be
uncompromising and unrelaxing in their claims, but rather
are anxious to meet the wishes of others, to respect and esteem
others. We ought not to approach each other with a coldly
calculating manner; we need mutual confidence and trust.
Confidence is not blind, but it always commits itself beyond
the measure of cool calculation. Love may be rewarded with
ingratitude, confidence may be misplaced and disappointed.
